components.title: acme-health-intake
components.description: Patient intake API on AWS (API Gateway -> Lambda -> DynamoDB + S3 uploads bucket), wrapped in a Terraform GRC baseline, an OPA/Rego policy gate, and a signed-evidence pipeline.
components.purpose: Accept patient intake submissions while meeting the SOC 2 criteria mapped below.
components.remarks: SOC 2 -> NIST 800-53 mapping used here (one representative control per criterion): CC6.1 -> sc-28 (encryption at rest), CC6.3 -> ac-6 (least privilege), CC6.6 -> sc-7 (boundary protection), CC6.7 -> sc-8 (transmission confidentiality), A1.2 -> cp-9 (system backup), CC7.2 -> si-4 (system monitoring). AICPA publishes no OSCAL catalog for the Trust Services Criteria, so NIST 800-53 Rev 5 is the catalog. Each pair was checked against the AICPA crosswalk 'Mapping: 2017 Trust Services Criteria to NIST 800-53' (2017 TSC with revised points of focus 2022, mapped to NIST 800-53 r5), which lists each of these controls under the corresponding criterion. That crosswalk is many-to-many: each criterion maps to further controls not selected here. Evidence objects live in an S3 Object Lock (GOVERNANCE, 90 days from 2026-09-18) vault, so they are protected until about 2026-12-17.

control-implementations.description: NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 controls satisfied (or planned) by the Acme Health intake service, each tagged with the SOC 2 Trust Services Criterion it supports.

links.text: AICPA crosswalk: 2017 Trust Services Criteria to NIST 800-53 (r5).

implemented-requirements.description: SOC 2 CC6.1 (GAP-01, GAP-02). Data at rest is encrypted under a customer-managed KMS key with rotation enabled: the uploads bucket (SSE-KMS), the DynamoDB submissions table, and the evidence vault all use the shared CMK. Encryption regressions are blocked at PR time by the cc61_s3_kms and cc61_dynamodb_kms Rego policies.

links.text: Signed pipeline bundle containing the terraform plan.json for the compliant baseline.

implemented-requirements.description: SOC 2 CC6.3 (GAP-07). The intake Lambda runs under a dedicated least-privilege role: its only data permissions are dynamodb:PutItem on the submissions table and s3:PutObject on the uploads bucket, replacing the starter's dynamodb:* / s3:* inline policy. Over-broad grants are blocked by the cc63_lambda_iam_least_privilege Rego policy.

links.text: Signed pipeline bundle containing the terraform plan.json for the compliant baseline.

implemented-requirements.description: SOC 2 CC6.6 (GAP-05). The intake Lambda runs inside the workload VPC's private subnets with a security group that allows no inbound traffic and HTTPS-only outbound, reaching AWS services through VPC endpoints (S3 and DynamoDB gateway endpoints, CloudWatch Logs interface endpoint) rather than the internet. Removing the VPC attachment is blocked by the cc66_lambda_vpc Rego policy.

links.text: Signed pipeline bundle containing the terraform plan.json for the compliant baseline.

implemented-requirements.description: SOC 2 CC6.7 (GAP-03). The uploads bucket has a bucket policy that denies any request where aws:SecureTransport is false, so data in transit to and from the bucket must use TLS. Removing the deny is blocked by the cc67_s3_tls_deny Rego policy.

links.text: Signed pipeline bundle containing the terraform plan.json for the compliant baseline.

implemented-requirements.description: SOC 2 A1.2 (GAP-04). Versioning is enabled on the uploads bucket, so overwritten or deleted patient uploads remain recoverable. Fixed in Terraform only: there is deliberately no Rego policy for this gap, since a single-resource remediation has no meaningful reintroduce-the-gap failure mode to test.

links.text: Signed pipeline bundle containing the terraform plan.json for the compliant baseline.

implemented-requirements.description: SOC 2 CC7.2 (GAP-06, GAP-08). KNOWN, UNREMEDIATED GAP: this control is planned, not implemented. Nothing in this service detects, alarms on, or analyses anomalies. Missing: Lambda reserved concurrency, dead-letter queue and X-Ray tracing (GAP-06); API Gateway access logging, throttling and WAF (GAP-08); CloudWatch alarms on Lambda errors and API 5xx/throttles; and a process for reviewing alerts. The only related capability is a multi-region CloudTrail trail (module.audit_trail.aws_cloudtrail.primary) with log-file validation, which is audit logging: the raw input a monitoring control would use, not monitoring itself. Note that AWS WAF does not attach to API Gateway HTTP APIs, so closing the WAF part of GAP-08 means changing the API type or fronting it with CloudFront.
